questions.q: What's wrong: 'NOTICE — I am happy to inform you all that we are having a very exciting and fun annual day celebration on 15th March at 10 am in the school auditorium and everyone should definitely come and bring their parents too!!!' (68 words)
questions.a: Nearly everything: first person, exclamations, no org name/date/heading/contact, 68 words, essay-tone. Correct: clipped third-person announcement under 50 words. A wrong answer listing only word-count shows the student sees the limit but not the register violations.

questions.q: Reorder a notice's header: heading, date, NOTICE, organization name.
questions.a: Organization name → NOTICE → date → heading. A wrong answer putting the heading first reveals the student treats the notice like an essay title instead of a bureaucratic instrument — the issuing authority leads because authority IS the format.

questions.q: Which body sentence fits a notice: 'You should totally come!' or 'Interested students may register with the undersigned by 10 March'?
questions.a: The second — third person, action + deadline + contact, zero enthusiasm-performance. A wrong answer choosing the first reveals the student hasn't internalized that notices inform; they never persuade.

questions.q: A notice is a public ______ in a box: organization name → NOTICE → date → heading → body answering What/When/Where/Who-contact → signature+designation.
Fill in the blank: A notice is a public ______ in a box: organization name → NOTICE → date → heading → body answering What/When/Where/Who-contact → signature+designation.
Fill in the blank: Show a real ______ notice, then strip it: everything outside the box is the skeleton, everything inside answers What-When-Where-Whom.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student drafts a complete notice under 50 words with all 6 elements, in third-person declaratives, with a body that answers the 4W questions, and can audit a defective notice for missing elements and register violations.
